License audit

Audited on 2026-11-04 (the source at 0ec6460, the SwiftPM checkout matching its lock file, the Web's lock file, Dawn's local build settings and the link rules it generated). On 2026-11-05, the ZIP and VM image of the published v0.2.0 were unpacked and checked, and the remaining work was taken forward.

Publishing Tsugumi's own code under MIT is compatible with the MIT / BSD licenses of Tree-sitter that were checked. The full license texts of what goes into the app's distributions have been bundled since v0.3.0 (what remains for distribution). The source corresponding to the GPL / LGPL software in the VM is placed on the boot disk's release (how the VM's corresponding source is provided).

This document records what could be confirmed from the code, the build steps and the artifacts. It is not a legal conclusion.

How strict to be

This is a project an individual publishes under MIT, distributing an ad hoc signed app on GitHub, so meeting what distribution requires comes first, without adding operational work.

TreatmentWhatWhy
MetFull texts and notices of what goes into the app and the VM, and the corresponding source of the VM's GPL / LGPL softwareThe licenses state these as conditions of distribution. They are built into the publishing and build scripts, adding no manual work
Left to declarations and upstream documentsThe license names of the VM's packages (nixpkgs' meta.license), and the license documents at the root of their sourcesAuditing the sources of 93 packages file by file is not worth the cost. It is stated that these are declarations, not audits
Resolved by removing11 unused maths fontsNot distributing them is surer and cheaper than checking them against upstream
Not pursued (with the reason kept)The full texts of dependencies inside plotly.js's minified build, and the full texts for web/dist, which the author does not distributeSee "Plotly's dependencies" below and the table
Not checkedDrift between the notices' versions and the pinsIt would add work at every dependency update. The full texts are copied from the checkout, so even with drift the texts distributed are right

Runtimetree-sitter 0.25.10 is MIT; SwiftTreeSitter 0.25.0 is BSD-3-ClauseListed separately

Julia's manifest does not include scanner.c, so only the scanner is copied into Grammars/TreeSitterJuliaScanner/ (with its LICENSE)Links to the LICENSE at the pinned revision, and the full license texts for copied queries

A list of license names alone, or a LICENSE in a checkout that exists only on the building machine, does not confirm that the text ships to recipients. For the original texts, see MIT and SwiftTreeSitter's LICENSE.

Dependencies easy to overlook

  • Swift Markdown / swift-cmark: Swift Markdown's LICENSE.txt is Apache-2.0 with the Swift runtime exception, and there is a NOTICE.txt too. swift-cmark's COPYING has, besides BSD-2-Clause, MIT notices for code derived from Houdini, GitHub, utf8proc and others. They must be kept in full, not omitted on the strength of one LICENSE name for the whole package.
  • SwiftMath and its fonts: SwiftMath's code is MIT, but the fonts it bundles are not. See the table below.
  • hosq: a library of the author's own, developed beforehand, is still a separate dependency. The LICENSE at the revision pinned in flake.lock is MIT. It is also stated in How it was built.
  • libgit2: linked by the core. The pinned nixpkgs definition specifies 1.9.7. It is GPLv2 with a special linking exception, so reading it simply as "GPL, so the whole app is GPL" is inaccurate. Following the upstream COPYING, distributing the combined executable is distinguished from distributing the library itself.
  • The Web's transitive dependencies: besides React and the like, loose-envify / js-tokens are in the lock file. commander is for the KaTeX CLI. What is in the lock file and what esbuild actually outputs are checked separately.
  • Dawn's transitive dependencies: a monolithic static library for Metal goes into the renderer dylib. Followed in "What Dawn actually takes in" below.

Apache-2.0 dependencies also cover NOTICE files and the like (Apache-2.0 §4).

What Dawn actually takes in

For Dawn 1716e88's libwebgpu_dawn.a (652 objects), the 1547 non-SDK files among the compile inputs recorded by ninja -t deps were examined. The only thing from third_party/ is Abseil; SPIRV-Tools and the like are not included.

IncludedFilesLicenseFull text bundled
Dawn / Tint themselves and generated code1244BSD-3-Clausedawn.LICENSE

Classified by the kind of copyright notice at the top of each file. The Apache-2.0 section of Dawn's LICENSE is for generator/templates/art/* and tools/android/webgpu/*, which are not included here. After changing Dawn's pin, build the renderer and review the breakdown of third_party/ with ninja -C build-renderer -t deps.

SwiftMath 1.7.3's fonts

The only font the app uses to draw maths is Latin Modern Math, the default of MTMathUILabel (macOS/Sources chooses no font; checked by test_licenses.py). Fonts are loaded when needed, and SwiftMath's MathFont.swift touches no other file. So macOS/build-app.sh removes the other 11 from the bundle. Distributions up to v0.2.0 contain all 12. That MTMathUILabel typesets maths with a bundle holding only Latin Modern was checked with a small executable that calls it the same way.

According to its upstream package, Latin Modern Math is under the GUST Font License, a form of the LPPL. Clause 2 of LPPL 1.3c treats distributing only part of the Work as a modification, so it can be read that the .otf and license in SwiftMath's bundle are not enough. The bundle's latinmodern-math.otf matches the one in the upstream latinmodern-math-1959.zip by SHA-256, so the whole upstream package, under 1 MB, is bundled as it is from the pinned nixpkgs' lmmath.src into licenses/fonts/latin-modern-math/.

The LICENSE of mathFonts.bundle at the pinned revision is MathChat's MIT notice, not a blanket license for the 12 fonts (a list read from each font's name table is in the Git history). GUST-FONT-LICENSE.txt refers to the conditions of LPPL 1.3c or later. The conditions of XITS and KpMath Sans were not checked against upstream; as they are no longer distributed, it was decided not to. If another font is used in future, it will be checked and bundled then.

The fonts of Help > Learn about Tsugumi

"Learn about Tsugumi" shows the documentation site's pages as they are, so its font is the same as in "The documentation site's font" below. macOS/build-app.sh copies it, with the full OFL text, into Contents/Resources/explainer/site/assets/.

How the VM's corresponding source is provided

The author's decision: the whole set is placed on the boot disk's release (gen740/tsugumi-vm). For each disk, macOS/tools/publish-vm.sh places sources.tar.gz (754 MiB for the current disk) and licenses.tar.gz on the same release as the binaries. The app's licenses/vm-boot/README.md has that URL. The release build stops for a disk not yet published, so it is never distributed unpublished.

The set is made by vm-source-bundle.py from the inventory.json that vm-inventory.py produced:

  • each package's source, and the patches it fetches (126)
  • nixpkgs at the pinned revision, with each package's configure, build and install steps and the patches inside nixpkgs
  • the parts of Tsugumi that assemble the disk (flake.nix, macOS/Container/ and so on), and the build instructions

Evaluating vm-boot from the unpacked set was confirmed to give the same store path as the published disk. Some of the archives (38) were also checked against the hashes in inventory.json. Whether rebuilding from scratch gives the same binaries has not been checked.

Confirmed facts
What is distributedThe contents of Tsugumi.zip and Tsugumi.dmg, and vmlinux and rootfs.erofs on the releases of gen740/tsugumi-vm
Contents103 store paths and the kernel: 93 packages. 37 of them include GPL or LGPL by nixpkgs' declarations (Linux, BusyBox, Bash, coreutils, glibc, Nix and others). Some are GPL-3.0, so GPLv3 §6 applies too
The kernel's generated configInside the binary (CONFIG_IKCONFIG) and as kernel-config in licenses.tar.gz

Two points remain open. These are not legal conclusions.

  • Where: GPLv2 §3 treats distribution by download as distributing the source if the source can be had from "the same place". vmlinux on its own is on the same release, but Tsugumi.zip and Tsugumi.dmg are on the releases of gen740/Tsugumi, another repository. GPLv3 §6(d) states that another server is fine if directions are given; GPLv2 has no such statement. As it is the same owner on the same GitHub, with the URL inside the app, the author chose this form.
  • Keeping it: while the binaries are distributed, their source is not deleted. When tidying the disk's releases, the app releases that carried that disk are checked too.

Published releases

The author's decision: fixed in v0.3.0; v0.1.0, v0.1.2 and v0.2.0 are not withdrawn. Their ZIPs have no full license texts (unpacking v0.2.0 found only the three documents in SwiftMath's bundle). The three tags have the same nixpkgs revision and vm-boot.nix, and v0.2.0's VM was confirmed by unpacking to be the same disk (v0.1.x were not unpacked), so the published VM source also corresponds to these versions.

Plotly's dependencies

plotly.min.js is the minified build upstream published, distributed as it is. The overall LICENSE and comments for some dependencies remain, but the full texts of the dependencies inside do not. For reference, resolving the dependencies of upstream's plotly.js@3.6.0 gives 258 packages, 31 without a license file. What actually goes into the bundle is a subset of these, and without upstream's metafile it is not known which.

Rather than keep by hand a list that includes unrelated things, it is distributed in upstream's form. To be strict, the full texts could be generated from the resolved dependencies and bundled (about 270 KB, and 31 by hand), or plotly.js could be bundled here to get a metafile. Vega's dependencies are in the lock file, so their full texts are bundled.

The VM is not exempt because "Nix fetches it"

The boot disk distributed contains GPL / LGPL binaries such as Linux (6.12.115, built with our own configuration in kernel.nix), Nix and Bash (the daemon and extra tools of vm-system.nix, and Cards' runtimes, are fetched after installation, so they are separate). Pinning nixpkgs in flake.lock, or showing how to fetch upstream sources, does not amount to distributing the source corresponding to these binaries (GPLv2 §3 includes the build and install scripts), and dynamic linking is no reason to skip checking either (LGPLv2.1 §§4–6).

The documentation site's font

Yusei Magic (SIL OFL 1.1), used for the handwriting in the figures on GitHub Pages, is placed in docs/site/assets/ as a WOFF subset of the characters the figures use (the Latin letters, digits and punctuation), together with the full OFL text. With no Reserved Font Name, it may be modified under the same name. Pages load it as Yusei Magic Subset.

Checking on updates

What stops by itself: missing full texts in the app, and boot disks not yet published (both stop the build). The boot disk's list and source are made by macOS/tools/publish-vm.sh, so nothing is generated by hand.

What people check: after updating dependencies, correct the versions in the notices. After changing Dawn's pin, review the breakdown of third_party/. Check the ZIP to be published one last time.
